label: copy-phase input b (fed-back b), stronger when the next output is z/r/b/p/3/g/f/o
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input token is b: 99.7% of activation mass is on in_tok=b, and it never fires during the original or delimiter phases. Plain (copy phase & input b) catches 99% of activations but only 15% precision, because most copy-phase b inputs stay silent. Two things decide whether a b fires and how strongly. (1) Position: it is rare before recall_idx 3 and strongest at recall_idx 4-5, i.e. when the b was a later original token. (2) The token being output next, i.e. the token that followed b in the original: z, r, b, p, 3 and g have the highest rates (about 7x lift), then f and o; outputs like k/l/j/h are weaker. All of the top-activating examples are b followed by r, z, b or p. The predicate scores dev F1 0.65 and mass recall 0.81. It misses weak activations on b followed by other tokens, and its false positives are b followed by a preferred token that still does not fire, often an earlier b. It does not fire on any other input token except for rare small activations on p and r.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: b, p, r, z, 3, -; least: j, i, t, y) and the token being output (most: z, b, r, p, 3, g; least: w, -, c, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=5, L=4 & t=6.
